findings.trigger: An individual message delete fails with anything other than discord.NotFound/discord.Forbidden (e.g. discord.HTTPException from a transient 500 or rate limit, or an IOError/OSError/RuntimeError) inside _individual_delete_messages - the fallback used by cleanup_channel's non-purge path (clean_sweep_bot_messages) and by _bulk_delete_messages' Forbidden/error fallback. The except at :389-390 only logs at DEBUG; it increments neither deleted_count nor permission_errors nor any other counter. cleanup_channel's success calc at :241 (`result.success = result.permission_errors == 0 and result.timeout_errors == 0`) therefore stays True even though that message was never deleted, so the caller is told the cleanup fully succeeded (`✅ CLEANUP SUCCESS`) while messages_deleted < messages_found - exactly the Z3 shape the same function's own comments at :237-241 and :248-259 already fixed for the permission-error and timeout cases, just missed for this third branch.
findings.suggestion: Count this branch too (e.g. add it to permission_errors, or a new counter folded into the same success check at cleanup_channel:241) instead of only logging it at DEBUG.

findings.trigger: delete_bot_messages_preserve_live_logs leaves max_age_days at its default of 30. _collect_messages (called first, gating whether cleanup_channel proceeds at all) applies that 30-day cutoff at :295-296. If at least one bot message younger than 30 days matches is_bot_but_not_preserved, cleanup_channel proceeds to _purge_with_filter, whose channel.purge(limit=request.message_limit, check=request.custom_filter) call at :405 has no age restriction of its own - only bot_only/custom_filter, scanned over the same message_limit history window. Any older (>30 day) bot messages in that window that also satisfy is_bot_but_not_preserved get deleted too, so result.purge_deleted can exceed result.messages_found and messages outside the max_age_days window are removed with nothing in the log or result showing it happened.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the unused max_age_days gate for the purge path and document that this method ignores age, or thread an equivalent age check into the purge's check callback so the gating step and the actual deletion can't drift apart.
findings.unsure_why: I could not run the code or inspect discord.py/py-cord's TextChannel.purge() implementation to independently confirm it applies no age limit beyond the check callback and message_limit; I also can't tell from this section whether max_age_days is meant to bound the purge path at all, or only the earlier gating step.

findings.trigger: get_channel_config_summary (def at :290, except at :307) and log_channel_update_decision (def at :357, except at :388) still catch only (RuntimeError, discord.Forbidden, discord.HTTPException, discord.NotFound) and (RuntimeError) respectively, while every other entry point in this same file - make_update_decision (:169), _should_recreate_message (:230), should_update_channel_overview (:351) - was broadened to `except Exception as e` under review D16, because a KeyError/TypeError from config parsing 'walked straight past' the narrower clause. If _get_channel_update_config (or global_config.get(...) inside it, e.g. when global_config is not the expected mapping) raises something like AttributeError or TypeError, get_channel_config_summary propagates it uncaught instead of returning its documented fallback dict, and log_channel_update_decision - which calls get_channel_config_summary - lets it propagate further out of a function meant purely for safe debug logging.
findings.suggestion: Broaden both except clauses to `except Exception as e`, matching the D16 fix already applied to the rest of this file.

findings.trigger: act_on_group only catches OSError around service.find(name)/service.members_of(name) (the group config lookup, :99-102). If the group config file is corrupted and the read path raises a JSON parse error (a ValueError subclass, not an OSError) - the same failure mode SPEC.md documents for load_server_order() elsewhere in this codebase ('Error loading server order: Expecting value: line 1 column 1', logged with the write silently returning []) - the exception propagates uncaught out of act_on_group instead of being turned into the GroupActionOutcome(False, refused=...) that the surrounding log line and every other error path in this function produce.
findings.suggestion: Catch whatever exception types services/config/group_service.py's read path can actually raise on a corrupted file (e.g. also ValueError/json.JSONDecodeError), not only OSError.
findings.unsure_why: services/config/group_service.py (get_group_service, .find, .members_of) is not part of this section's source, so I can't confirm it can raise something other than OSError on a corrupted file - only that the equivalent config-read pattern elsewhere in this codebase (load_server_order, per SPEC.md Z7) is documented as raising JSONDecodeError rather than OSError.

notes: cleanup_channel (services/discord/channel_cleanup_service.py:199) is touched by both F1 (via clean_sweep_bot_messages / the non-purge delete path) and F2 (via delete_bot_messages_preserve_live_logs / the purge path); the verdict entry cites F1 as the primary finding since it is the higher-confidence, higher-severity one. services/discord/embed_helper_service.py:118 get_translations carries an in-code comment (review D15) describing a cross-file cache-key mismatch: two different callers of translation_manager (status_handlers.py's `config.get('language', 'de')` vs get_current_language()'s `config.get('language', 'en')`) can disagree about the default language, which - if true - would let English strings get cached under a 'translations_de' key and stay there. That defect, if it exists, lives in status_handlers.py / translation_manager.py, neither of which is in this section's source, so I left the verdict as 'checked' (the code in this file itself, using an explicit `lang` parameter throughout, is internally consistent) rather than guessing at unseen code. services/docker_service/docker_action_service.py:112 execute_docker_action's cache-invalidation try/except (around line 222) also catches a specific tuple rather than Exception; I did not raise this as a finding because I cannot see services/status/status_cache_service.py or services/infrastructure/container_status_service.py to know what they can actually raise, and the surrounding review comments (E45, E50) suggest this file has already had close attention to exactly this class of bug.
